h1: The 7 Best Printer Tables for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven printer tables and file-cabinet stands for home offices, compared on tabletop size, storage, casters and cable management.
summary: The HUANUO printer stand is the best printer table for a home office: a rear cable channel, locking casters and a storage drawer for $25 to $50. The YAOHUOO has the larger 22 by 15 inch top, and the VASAGLE is a labeled two-drawer file cabinet. The DEVAISE and Letaya are storage-first cabinets.
intro: Printer tables usually fail on a measurement buyers forget to take: the printer body plus the room its paper tray and scanner lid need to open. A table that fits the printer closed ends up blocking the lid, or leaves the tray hanging in the air. Measure with everything extended before you look at a single listing, and keep a few inches spare on each side.

We reviewed seven printer tables and file-cabinet stands from their listings, ranking them on tabletop size, storage, mobility, cable routing and how clearly each is labeled for printer use. Several picks are file cabinets with a flat top, so we flag where the top surface is the limit. Dimensions and drawer counts come from the listings and owner reports.

products.name: HUANUO Printer Stand with Cable Management and Storage Drawer
products.verdict: A purpose-built printer table with real cable routing and a drawer.
products.description:
The HUANUO is a printer stand with a dedicated rear cable management channel, locking caster wheels and a storage drawer under the top shelf. It stands at a maximum of 14.1 inches tall, suits compact and mid-size printers, and sells for $25 to $50. A rear channel keeps the power cord and USB or network cable from snagging when you roll the stand out for a paper jam.

It finishes first because it deals with the two problems that plague printer setups: tangled cords and a table that drifts. The YAOHUOO has a larger top, but the HUANUO is the better organized of the two. Against the VASAGLE, it costs less and rolls under a desk.

Buy it for a desk-side or under-desk setup with a standard home printer. The caveat is the compact top, which will not suit a large business machine.
products.idealFor: Home offices with a compact or mid-size printer.
products.skipIf: You own a large business all-in-one.

products.name: YAOHUOO 22x15 Large Printer Stand with Drawer
products.verdict: A 22 by 15 inch top for business-class all-in-one printers.
products.description:
The YAOHUOO is a two-tier rolling cart with a 22 inch wide by 15 inch deep tabletop, a built-in storage drawer and casters. It is described as suited to business-class all-in-one printers and sells for $25 to $50. A bigger top matters because the scanner lid and paper trays need clearance, and a tight fit leaves a lid stuck against the wall.

It ranks second because the listing says less about cable management than the HUANUO does. The larger top is the reason to pick it, since it gives a full-size printer room for open lids and trays. Against the VASAGLE, it offers a wider surface at a lower price, though no file drawers.

Choose it if your printer is a full-size machine. The caveat is that it takes more floor room. Measure the printer with its trays extended before ordering, and skip it if floor space is very tight.

products.name: VASAGLE CUSTOS 2-Drawer File Cabinet Printer Stand
products.verdict: A small file cabinet labeled and sized for printers.
products.description:
The VASAGLE CUSTOS is a two-drawer file cabinet measuring 15.7 inches wide, 16.5 inches deep and 27.6 inches tall, in matte black. It is marketed as a printer stand, has a rolling base, and its drawers take A4 and Letter documents. It sells for $50 to $100. Being labeled for printers is a signal that the top suits a typical home machine.

It sits third because its 15.7 inch width is narrower than the YAOHUOO's 22 inch top, so large machines will overhang. In exchange, it adds a proper pair of filing drawers, which the open stands lack. Against the GYIIYUO, it is more rigid, though smaller on top.

Good for small home offices that need a compact printer table plus file space. The caveat is the narrow surface: check your printer's width against 15.7 inches. Skip it if your printer is wider than 15 inches.
products.idealFor: Small offices needing filing and a printer top.
products.skipIf: Your printer is wider than 15 inches.

products.name: GYIIYUO 2 Drawer File Cabinet with 24-inch Extended Desktop
products.verdict: A 24 inch extended desktop with two fabric-front drawers.
products.description:
The GYIIYUO is a mobile file cabinet with a 24 inch extended desktop surface, two fabric-front drawers that fit A4 and Letter files, a side storage bag and a rolling base. It sells for $50 to $100. The extended top gives you a place for the printer plus a stack of paper or a laptop, making it a small rolling workstation.

It lands fourth because fabric-front drawers are less rigid than the metal and wood cabinets above, though the 24 inch top is larger than the VASAGLE's. It trades sturdiness for a more flexible surface, and the side bag holds supplies a drawer would not.

Pick it if you want a mobile printer-and-paper station with extra desk space. The caveat is the drawer construction, so look closely at how the fabric fronts hold up. Skip it if you want rigid metal drawers.
products.idealFor: Mobile work stations that need extra surface.

products.name: HOOBRO 2-Tier Printer Stand with Charging Station
products.verdict: An open two-tier stand with a built-in charging station shelf.
products.description:
The HOOBRO is a two-tier open shelf printer stand with a charging station shelf, a rustic brown and black finish, and a height low enough to fit under many desks. It sells for $25 to $50. A charging shelf keeps phones and tablets close to the printer, which suits a shared desk where devices pile up, and open shelves hold ream-sized paper.

It ranks fifth because it has no drawer and no wheels listed, unlike the HUANUO. The charging shelf is the distinctive feature, but it does not help if you want to roll the printer out for a jam. Against the YAOHUOO, it is lighter on features at the same price tier.

Choose it if you want open shelf storage and a charging spot. The caveat is no closed storage, so use a drawer model for files. Skip it if you need closed storage.
products.idealFor: Desks needing device charging near the printer.

products.name: DEVAISE 3-Drawer Mobile File Cabinet
products.verdict: Three lateral file drawers with a wide, stable top.
products.description:
The DEVAISE is a three-drawer lateral file cabinet in a rustic brown finish, with rolling casters and a wide, stable flat top. It sells for $50 to $100. Lateral drawers hold files side to side, which suits letter and legal paper, and a wide top carries a large laser or inkjet all-in-one without overhang.

It takes the sixth spot because it is storage first and printer table second, with no printer-specific features like cable management. The wide top is the saving grace for larger machines. Against the VASAGLE, it holds more paperwork in the same price bracket but lacks the printer label.

Buy it if you have a lot of paperwork and want a printer to sit on top. The caveat is the lack of cable routing. Skip it if you only need a small stand, or if cable routing matters more.
products.idealFor: Offices with heavy paperwork and a big printer.
products.skipIf: You only need a small printer stand.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock
products.verdict: Three lockable metal drawers, assembled on arrival.
products.description:
The Letaya is a metal mobile file cabinet with three lockable drawers that fit Letter, Legal and A4 documents. It ships fully assembled and fits under a desk. It sells for $50 to $100. Locking drawers matter when paperwork holds tax or client records and the printer sits in a shared space.

It ranks last as a printer table because the top is not marketed for printers and the listing is silent on top size. Its edge is the lock, which the other cabinets here do not name. Against the DEVAISE, it lists less about its top, so you cannot confirm whether a large printer fits.

Choose it if you store private paperwork near your printer. The caveat is the missing top dimensions, so confirm the top is large enough for your machine before ordering. Skip it if you need a confirmed printer-sized top.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed printer-sized top.

whatMatters.detail: The top must hold the printer body and leave room for trays and lids to open. A table that is exactly printer-sized will feel cramped, and overhanging trays jam. Measure your printer with all trays out and compare with the listed width and depth. The YAOHUOO lists 22 by 15 inches, the VASAGLE 15.7 inches wide.

whatMatters.factor: Height and fit under a desk
whatMatters.detail: A table that slides under your desk saves floor space but may place the printer too low to reach comfortably. A taller cabinet puts controls at hand. Check the listed height against your desk clearance, such as the HUANUO's 14.1 inch maximum, and consider whether you will stand or sit when you use the printer.

A printer needs both a power cord and a USB or network cable. A rear channel keeps those from snagging and from being pulled out when the table moves. Look for a named cable routing feature in the listing, as on the HUANUO. Most cabinets here have none, so plan on cable clips, and keep power and data cords apart where possible.

Wheels let you roll the printer out for paper jams, but unlocked wheels can drift. Locking casters keep the table put. Check whether the listing says locking, as the HUANUO does. A rolling cabinet with unlocked wheels will creep every time you pull out a tray or lift a lid, and a drifting printer can pull its own cables loose.

A heavy laser all-in-one can exceed what a thin shelf supports. The listing may give a limit in pounds. Compare it to the printer's weight on its spec page, and leave margin. Cabinets such as the DEVAISE and Letaya are generally sturdier than open stands, but check their top rating, since a drawer-load rating does not always match the top.

faq.q: How do I know if a printer table will fit my printer?
faq.a: Measure the printer's width and depth with trays and lids open. Compare to the table's listed top size, such as the YAOHUOO's 22 by 15 inches, and keep a few inches spare on every side so the lid can swing.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying a table that only fits the printer closed. Open trays and scanner lids need space too, so a 15.7 inch VASAGLE top that suits a small printer will hold a large one badly, and open trays then hang in the air.

faq.q: Is a file cabinet worth it over an open stand?
faq.a: If you store paperwork, yes. The VASAGLE gives printer height and drawers together. If not, an open stand like the HUANUO or HOOBRO costs less and keeps the printer closer to hand, with nothing to open or unlock.

faq.q: How do I set up a printer table?
faq.a: Assemble the frame, lock the casters, place the printer and route cables through the channel if offered. Leave room around vents, and give the HUANUO's rear channel a clear run to the wall. Level the table before loading it.

Hard plastic wheels can mark soft flooring. Use a mat or choose wheels with soft treads, and keep locking casters engaged so the table does not scrape when you open a tray. Felt pads also help on hardwood.

faq.q: Why are some picks file cabinets?
faq.a: Many home offices need paper storage near the printer. We included cabinets such as the DEVAISE and Letaya with a flat top and noted where the top size is the limit, so you can check it against your own printer's width.

finalTake: Buy the HUANUO for a compact or mid-size printer, since it handles cords and wheels well. Take the YAOHUOO for a business-class all-in-one, and the VASAGLE if you need filing under a small printer. The GYIIYUO suits a mobile workstation, the HOOBRO a charging shelf, and the DEVAISE and Letaya heavy paperwork. Measure the printer with trays open first.
